openings.claim: Switching may disrupt selection/checking or shape-to-role mapping.
openings.discriminator: Staging reduces selection/checking, sparing insertion; placement cards reduce switch-related orientation corrections/retries.
openings.probe: Counterbalance repeated/alternating sequences and staging/card comparisons across workers/layouts; time four stages including overhead; reconcile contents independently.
openings.uncertainty: Complexity confounds switching; reports cannot establish shortages.

openings.claim: Specific slot maps may resolve short-partition uncertainty.
openings.discriminator: Fewer questions/more unaided successes implicate instructions; persistence suggests fit/placement ambiguity.
openings.probe: Compare generic/specific diagrams with ten participants, matched layouts, verified kits.

openings.claim: Pairing/sequence may explain retries despite overlapping widths.
openings.discriminator: Pairing/stage clustering persists under repetition; sequence alters retries without switching.
openings.probe: Identify parts/slots; counterbalance sequences across workers/layouts; compare D1; monitor wear, stopping affected comparisons.
openings.uncertainty: Mechanisms may coexist; dismantling may alter fit.

decision: Screen within 15 shared samples and fixed delivery slack. Preserve footprint, assortment, removable joints, ordered counts/colors; verify 500 initial/0.40 recurring ceilings. Repeated-order times keep preassembly plausible. Synthetic evidence establishes no remedy; pilot targets remain unverified.
